## Changes since 9.3.0-dzbarsky36

- Reduce Starlark call allocations: use smaller frames for builtin calls, remove redundant builtin names, and reuse builtin and Starlark frames in separate per-thread pools ([#73](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/73), [#74](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/74), [b51f5477](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/b51f5477a8c8bc37c29147b8e9826c891205a5f9)).
- Avoid allocating streams to read the main aspect, cache rule-class logging names per `RuleContext.Builder`, and avoid wrapping ordinary attribute lookups in `AttributeResolutionResult` ([#70](https://github.com/dzbarsky/bazel/pull/70), [ae283f33](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/ae283f33e3bcb40cda469412acfc702149e1b034), [4e1c9b4d](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/4e1c9b4dd5c54599bf70e73797f659d15d614192)).
- Avoid allocation and synchronization when `SkyKeyPool.getOrWeakIntern` finds an existing key ([dba37383](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/dba373838f6302c9298bff4f86e234c879cd6a8c)).
- Share configuration-independent toolchain declarations across configurations while retaining this release branch's early toolchain-type and target-platform filtering. Evaluate target settings in the requesting configuration and preserve visibility, test-only, and deprecation checks ([#31301](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31301)).
- Propagate analysis-phase visibility and test-only flags to no-config targets ([#31309](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31309)).
- Fix a null-pointer crash when wildcard toolchain registration matches non-rule targets ([#28711](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/28711)).

### Compatibility

`toolchain` declarations no longer accept the previously ineffective `features` and `aspect_hints` attributes. Remove those attributes from `toolchain` targets ([#31312](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/31312)).

### Validation

All 16 targeted Starlark, Skyframe, package, platform, toolchain, configuration, producer, aspect, and serialization test targets passed on Linux remote execution against the release branch. Tests cover frame reuse, analysis-flag propagation, shared toolchain declarations, early filtering, and wildcard registration.

Linux and macOS prebuilts for x86_64 and arm64 are built and version-checked before immutable publication, with SHA-256 checksums and build-provenance records. Existing release tags and assets are preserved.
